head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: Failed check lookups now report a gh failure and preserve HTTP status when available, with little added maintenance cost. Regression evidence supports the fix; live rate-limit behavior and realized user benefit remain unverified.
reasons: The change addresses issue #656 directly: empty output from a failed check lookup now produces a gh failure instead of an invalid-JSON error. Required-check errors retain the parsed HTTP status.
Scope stays within the reported failure. The change reuses existing error handling, adds no dependencies or configuration, and introduces little maintenance cost. No instruction files changed.

Reported evidence includes a regression that failed before the fix, passing focused tests, 3454 passing tests with clean RuboCop results, and a live missing-PR lookup. One review round found only a missing direct test for empty stdout with exit 8.

Verification is proportionate to a diagnostic change shared by status, watch, handoff, and merge. Lookup failures continue to raise; reverting restores the prior behavior without persistent data changes.

A live rate limit and end-to-end rate-limit handling through each consuming command were not reported as exercised. Empty stdout with exit 8 lacks a direct test. Messages without an '(HTTP nnn)' marker retain a nil status. Incident frequency and realized user benefit remain unknown.
alternative: Keep the bounded fix. A direct empty-stdout exit-8 test could add coverage, but the reported evidence does not justify broader error parsing or new workflow behavior.
next_action: Carry the existing validation and known coverage limits into the PR recommendation.
